long_biography.plain_text:
The Strip's first modern megaresort changed the economics and imagery of Las Vegas by treating the casino as one element of a larger theatrical destination. Steve Wynn financed the project through mainstream capital markets, surrounding gaming with rooms, restaurants, entertainment and a street-facing volcano. Its success triggered a wave of large-scale construction and made spectacle central to the city's visitor economy.

Wynn deepened that approach at Bellagio, combining high-end hospitality with fountains, a conservatory, boutiques and a public gallery displaying works from his collection. After selling his first resort company to MGM, he returned with the namesake Wynn Las Vegas and expanded into Macau. His developments placed architecture, service, entertainment and art within a single designed experience.
